In Southeast Asia, generative AI has become an essential part of daily life, actively used by 243 million people (58% of the working population) and scaling four times faster than the rollout of the mobile internet. This has major implications for the region’s economy, according to the 11th edition of the annual e-Conomy SEA report 1 . Building the Intelligent Econom y, by Google, Temasek, and Bain & Company, finds that widespread AI implementation is propelling the region’s digital economy to grow 17% year-on-year (YoY) to reach $368 billion 2 in Gross Merchandise Value (GMV) in 2026. This puts it firmly on track to exceed $1 trillion by 2035. Using tokens 3 as the new benchmark for the AI economy, the report projects that growing confidence in agentic commerce will drive a 60-fold surge in regional AI usage over the next five years.

Here are the three key takeaways from this year's e-Conomy SEA 2026 report:

## 1. AI is sustaining growth in every sector.

Across the digital economy, AI is reshaping how people live, shop, and move. E-commerce ($226B GMV, +18% YoY) anchors this shift, as shoppers use multimodal discovery and in-app assistants to confidently navigate complex purchases. These personalized experiences organically drive 10% higher conversions and order volume uplifts as large as 75%.

In online travel ($59B GMV, +10% YoY), traditional search engines remain the top platform people use to plan travel, while generative AI has overtaken social media to become the second-most used tool for organizing complex itineraries.

Online media ($44B revenue, +22% YoY) is personalizing content feeds and connecting audiences with more relevant ads, yielding a 10 to 20% quality engagement uplift as commerce media becomes a $4 billion market.

Mobility and food delivery ($40B GMV, +15% YoY) saves consumers time via predictive suggestions, smarter routing, and AI-powered offerings like pooled rides, fueling healthy transactional growth.

Finally, digital financial services ($1,650B GTV, +16% YoY) help consumers with real-time fraud detection, broader credit access, and personalized financial recommendations that complement human advice, alongside Singapore’s regional leadership in digital wealth platforms.

## 2. Consumer trust will help unlock the era of agentic commerce.

Digital automation is already well established across the region, where 72% of users rely on everyday features like price tracking. This familiarity is clearing the runway for agentic commerce, with 75% expressing willingness to let AI agents autonomously compare prices and complete transactions on their behalf.

This momentum is rooted in regional optimism: people in Southeast Asia view AI as a net benefit to society, with 62% reporting greater trust in AI tools today than a year ago. Driven by proven track records (56%), rising familiarity (55%), and output accuracy (53%), this trust signals a clear runway for deeper platform integration. To feel comfortable using new agentic capabilities, users expect clarity and guardrails, including robust privacy safeguards (44%), transparent information on what AI can and cannot do (36%), and the ability to reverse agentic transactions (30%).

## 3. Four major areas must adapt to enable AI adoption.

To support a projected 60-fold increase in regional AI usage by 2030, the region's broader digital ecosystem must systematically evolve across four critical conditions:

- Accelerated agentic adoption and sustainable economics: Businesses need to move beyond using AI to answer single questions and start using it to help complete multi-step tasks from start to finish, backed by strong privacy safeguards and clear safety rules. At the same time, running AI models must keep getting more affordable and deliver clear, practical value, so businesses of all sizes can adopt the technology sustainably.

- Scaled physical infrastructure : Physical expansion must rapidly keep pace with soaring compute demand. Meeting this trajectory requires a ~3x expansion in data center capacity over the next five years, with AI workloads capturing a dominant share of total infrastructure.

- Strict model and energy efficiency : National frameworks, such as Singapore’s binding Power Usage Effectiveness (PUE) rules under the Digital Infrastructure Bill, must guide next-generation facilities, paired with expanded clean energy access like Malaysia’s Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS) model.

- Unified regional governance : Anchoring this trajectory, the upcoming ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement (DEFA) in November 2026 will establish the world's first region-wide digital trade pact, providing a framework that can unlock further growth in the Southeast Asia digital economy.

How can artists use technology to deepen our understanding of life, matter, and consciousness? That’s the question two artists sought to answer during the Online Artist Residency with LAS Art Foundation in collaboration with Google Arts & Culture.

## “nom nom” by Xin Liu

In “nom nom,” Xin explores how collective intelligence naturally arises when millions of small particles interact. To craft the project, she drew on research into artificial life and emergent computation by Googler researchers Blaise Agüera y Arcas and Alexander Mordvintsev , and the concept of Neural Cellular Automata (NCAs) — models where millions of particles form, compete, and dissolve into a living ecology. Eunjo’s “techno-alchemy” process bridges ancient philosophy, linguistics, and modern psychology. She sees technology as a medium that reveals the philosophical and psychological underpinnings of our physical and digital existence.

For this project, Eunjo converted hand-drawn sketches into 3D assets using Nano Banana and Veo. She then layered motion-captured choreography onto characters and mapped Korean Hangul phonetics over the 3D environment to create a linguistic system that reflected the landscape’s geometry.

“This commission opened up a vast alchemical laboratory,” Eunjo says. “As the [Buddhist] philosophy of Indra's net posits that all entities reflect one another to form a colossal web, this concept manifests today through the neural network.”

Google Quantum AI has demonstratively opened up a key bottleneck in quantum computing: we’ve shown that “magic state cultivation” works in practice on our Willow processor, reducing errors about 40x compared to without it. This breakthrough, published today in Science , is a crucial step towards scaling up quantum computing to practical use.

## The "magic state" bottleneck

Since 2004, long before quantum computing was a practical engineering pursuit, researchers have foreseen a particularly tricky bottleneck.

To achieve “universal” quantum computing and execute useful programs, you need to be able to run (and error-correct ) a specific set of quantum operations. You can do this by first creating what are called "magic states," so dubbed because they can help you create the operations you need for going beyond classical computing.

But there’s a catch: creating high-quality, error-corrected magic states is incredibly resource-heavy. Some estimates have shown that up to 95% of a quantum computer’s entire capacity might need to be dedicated to making them — leaving little room for actual computing. An extra challenge is that once you use a magic state, you can’t re-use it, making magic states a scarce resource.

So for 20 years, researchers have been chipping away at this cost of magic, bringing it lower and lower.

## How we made this breakthrough

In 2024, Google Quantum AI researchers Craig Gidney, Noah Shutty, and Cody Jones harnessed an idea from the literature, refined it, and developed what we now call “magic state cultivation.” Their approach promised an especially large reduction. The idea was that cultivation would act like a filter. You would inject a noisy state into a small region on a quantum chip, and then run a series of highly coordinated measurements to check for errors and remove any flawed attempts. Craig and team showed how that would let you grow, or “cultivate,” an exceptionally pure, low-error quantum state that you could simultaneously adapt into a larger, useful encoding.

On paper, it looked great. If we could make this idea actually work on our quantum hardware, it could substantially reduce the size of the quantum computer needed for practical tasks.

In practice — and on par with developing many new technologies — it required a whole series of technical innovations and engineering.

As just one example, when first testing the cultivation protocol, Google Quantum AI research scientist Emma Rosenfeld was seeing data that seemed to defy the laws of physics. After months of confusion, simulations, discussions with colleagues, and consistency checks, she found that it arose from an incorrect assumption in the team’s go-to measurement technique. Specifically, a particular kind of noise in the lab caused by electrical equipment drift and temperature variation was interfering with the benchmark’s validity. The solution required a pivot in both our theoretical and engineering approaches. The team added extra control to the system to reduce the impact of that noise, and invented a new benchmarking technique to solve the issue more fundamentally, by using cultivation as a tool to measure itself.

With this and many more algorithmic innovations and engineering solutions, we established a new state-of-the-art in quantum metrology. On Google Quantum AI's Willow processor, our protocol achieved an extraordinary 40-fold reduction in errors relative to un-cultivated states. And we got T-states with a record logical fidelity of 99.99%.

Now published in Science , this work is the first demonstration of a practical solution to one of quantum computing's most severe resource bottlenecks. It demonstrates, on real hardware, that we can efficiently create these crucial magic states.

## Our findings and the future

We also took the first steps in demonstrating that Craig and others’ theories are compatible with our quantum computing architecture. We learned how to successfully switch between “color codes” (one newer type of quantum error correction, ideal for cultivation) and “surface codes” (another, more established method), grafting states from a distance-3 color code to a distance-5 surface code. Originally developed in the 2024 theory paper, this grafting protocol showed that in practice, purified states can survive and transfer smoothly inside our hardware.

Of course, we still need to demonstrate magic state cultivation at a larger scale to make it realistic for practical quantum computing, and plenty of technical challenges remain. But this achievement takes a key theoretical idea and turns it into an experimentally demonstrated reality. It brings us one step closer to our goal at Google Quantum AI : building a useful, error-corrected quantum computer to solve otherwise unsolvable problems.

For technology to be truly impactful, school leaders and educators must lead the way. That’s why we’re expanding our free Google AI Educator Series to all 650,000 educators in the UK and Ireland. This program helps educators build confidence to responsibly use this technology to craft engaging lesson plans, simplify administrative tasks, and tailor lesson plans to diverse learning needs.

Initially launched to 6 million educators across the U.S. and recently expanded to India and Korea , the content is delivered via teacher-led virtual and in-person events. The practical, bite-sized curriculum is built by educators, for educators. Teachers can immediately apply these lessons to personalize instruction, safely guide students, and reclaim vital teaching time . Upon completing modules, teachers earn micro-credentials and badges to showcase their AI literacy.

In the UK, analysis from Public First found that almost three quarters (74%) of roles in education have the potential to be enhanced by AI. The AI Works for Britain report highlights a growth opportunity: while 15% of the UK is already saving time with this technology, there is untapped potential to scale. The Google AI Educator Series equips teachers with similar upskilling opportunities, and teachers trained on this program will contribute towards the UK government’s goal of training 10 million workers in digital skills by 2030.

We’ve also partnered with the National Governance Association to create an AI Policy Toolkit , helping school governors and trustees safely adopt AI policy, tools and training. This toolkit and the Google AI Educator Series align with our goal to ensure educators and school leaders are equipped with essential digital literacy skills for the modern classroom.

Gemini 4 Argon , our new frontier model, excels at tackling complex projects. Argon excels at deep work in complex, real-world tasks to help across domains including coding, finance, legal, cybersecurity, and science. Its depth and precision across multi-step tasks leads Argon to outperform other frontier models on benchmarks across domains.

Since we rolled out Argon broadly last week, we've seen builders tap into its expanded abilities to create interactive tools, engineer 3D worlds, and more. With major upgrades in spatial reasoning, mathematical precision, and visual coding, Gemini 4 Argon can generate complex 3D environments. In this test by Lumina (@LuminaBench on X) , Argon rendered a 3D simulation of a seaplane with realistic lighting, reflections, and water movement. Because Argon can maintain depth and precision across multi-step tasks, it was able to coordinate the motions of different elements simultaneously.

## Map wildfires and tectonic shockwaves on a 3D globe.

Gemini 4 Argon excels at turning dense, unstructured data into clear visuals. Using Gemini 4 Argon in Antigravity, Alex Patrascu (@maxescu on X) combined NASA's live feed of global wildfires and seismic data from the U.S. Geological Survey to create an interactive 3D globe. Argon translated the image into a complex rendering with functioning doors and windows, flickering oil lamps, and an undercarriage that reacts to bumps in the road.

## Create a multiplayer capture-the-flag game.

Chong-U (@chongdashu on X) used Gemini 4 Argon to build “Backyard Rascals,” a multiplayer browser game where cartoon animals race to capture the other team’s flag. Argon's ability to maintain depth and precision across complex workflows helped this creator build a game with complex features allowing the characters to run, collide, whack each other, and cheer as multiple players engage in real time.

Sydney Bordonaro styles top professional athletes, turning the pregame tunnel into a must-watch runway. But because her roster is scattered across the country, being in the same room as clients for a fitting rarely happens. That makes her biggest challenge selling the vision. A photo of a jacket tells a player nothing about how the outfit actually looks on them, and when they can't see the idea, it’s easy to say no. That’s why Sydney uses Gemini to bring her ideas to life before an outfit ever ships.

Here’s how she builds looks for clients from hundreds of miles away:

## 1. Visualize the look.

Sydney uploads pictures of the clothes she sources to visualize them on her client directly in Gemini. It keeps the player looking like herself while showing how the full outfit comes together on her.

Try it yourself: Upload a photo of yourself alongside screenshots of items you want to buy. Gemini combines them into a single image so you can see how the full outfit looks before ordering.

## 2. Swap individual pieces.

Styling rarely lands on the first try. Sydney simply talks to Gemini to tweak details like swapping boots for loafers or cropping a jacket without having to start over from scratch.

Try it yourself: Instead of writing a new prompt, ask for single adjustments like "keep this outfit, but change the jacket to dark denim."

## 3. Get a second opinion.

Once the look comes together, Sydney sends the picture directly to her client. Seeing the complete fit builds confidence, often turning a hesitant "maybe" into a quick yes for bolder style choices.

Try it yourself: Test outfit ideas for upcoming weddings, job interviews, or trips and share them with friends for a gut check before you commit.

Beyond building outfits, Sydney uses Gemini as a quick problem-solver. When an unexpected makeup smudge lands on a client’s collar right before an event, snapping a quick picture brings up specific, step-by-step instructions to clean it using stuff Sydney already has in the room.

Try it yourself: Take a photo of a clothing stain and ask Gemini how to clean it using what you have around the house.

As the holiday season kicks into high gear, the Universal Cart is just one way we’re giving shoppers the convenience and smarts they need to make the best shopping choices.
